comments.content: The logging statement passes two arguments (`s` and `renderer`) but the message `"Assertion `{}` failed!"` has only one placeholder. The `renderer` value will be silently ignored. Either add a placeholder (e.g. `"Assertion `{}` failed! Rendered value: `{}`"`) or remove the extra argument.

Reading `this.conditions.getExpression()` bypasses the standard Property rendering pipeline and assumes the raw expression is always a JSON array literal. If `conditions` is provided as a Pebble expression that resolves to a list, `getExpression()` will return the unrendered template string and JSON parsing will fail. Prefer using `runContext.render(this.conditions).asList(String.class)` to properly resolve the property, then render each item.

Using `isFalsy` instead of `!isTruthy` changes semantics: a rendered value that is `null` will be treated as neither falsy nor a success (since `isFalsy(null)` returns false, the else branch increments success). A null/empty render likely indicates an assertion problem and would be counted as a success here. Consider using `!TruthUtils.isTruthy(renderer)` so empty/null values are correctly treated as failures per the documented boolean coercion (`''` coerces to false).

The example YAML contains a malformed line: `"  - id: fail\n" +
" +` embeds a literal `
" +` inside the flow definition. This will produce a broken example in the generated documentation. Fix to `"  - id: fail
" +`.

This appears to be an accidental edit that corrupted the example: `{{ outputs.output_values.²}}` replaced the previous valid expression `{{ outputs.output_values.values.taskrun_data }}`. The `²` character is clearly unintended. Please revert this line.

Throwing a raw `java.lang.Exception` is discouraged. Consider throwing a more specific exception type (e.g., `IllegalStateException` or a Kestra-specific exception) to convey the assertion failure semantics more clearly.
